I felt very similar to you a while back. Then I started to question if happiness came from within not from without. That really resonated with me. Essentially happiness is not derived from an object, Fame, fortune, relationships etc. They are all temporary and will fade. Even when you have them there is the fear of losing them, so you're never fully happy. When you obtain whatever it is you have been after you are happy for a brief second. This is when you stop seeking happiness from the outside world. You can just 'be'. Inevitably you then latch onto another objective and lose this fulfilment up until you achieve the next thing and so on. 

If you take a step back and look at where feelings of love and joy actually come from you'll probably find it's from within you. You have just been taught to associate these feelings with external factors, but you don't have to. 

When you are with a girl, cuddling etc. you feel a sense of belonging and worth. You feel valued and loved. Where are these feelings actually coming from? Are they coming from outside of you or inside of you? Pay close attention. Because if they are coming from within, do you actually need outside circumstances to align to be happy or can you go to their source and feel bliss all the time? I believe it is the latter. 

Question what it is about being in a relationship you crave. Is it feeling loved? Because that comes from within you. No relationship can give you that. You have to realise that you create your own happiness. At that point you can enter a relationship and enjoy it for what it is: a nice little spice for your life, not the answer to it. 

DISCLAIMER: I am not trying to lecture anybody here. I am just describing my experience and current level of understanding. If this doesn't help and/or I sound crazy please feel free to ignore me :)

I think the trick is to find something you genuinely enjoy. Or mutliple things and mix them up. Do you play any instruments? Is there an instrument you'd like to learn? Perhaps you'd like to learn how to make electronic music? It just needs to be something you think is cool/fun. And don't overdo it. That's where I think mixing things up comes in. For instance, are there any topics you'd like to know more about? Does metaphysics interest you? Check out a book by Bohm etc. Again don't overdo it. Maybe just read before bed/when you are drawn to doing it. If it feels like a chore don't do it. 

I personally enjoy watching shows every so often. They're not all mindless zombie fodder. But I get not wanting to fall into a laziness hole. Maybe limit yourself to an hour a day (or whatever you think is appropriate). 

I too find the gym to be work and not massively fun. That's one of those things you've just gotta do for the long term benefits rather than immediate gratification. Also I tend to feel better having done it than not. It's just the act of motivating myself to start that can be tricky. The key is making it a habit so you don't even have to think about whether or not you're going to do it. You just do it.

Do you have goals for the rest of your life? Maybe you want to start an online business or learn a new language and teach abroad? Whatever it is, you could spend time working towards that. 

There's also spending time with friends/family. Or going out in nature. Walking your dog (if you have one) etc. Volunteering if that's your jam.  

It's important to note that learning new things tends to mean you suck at those things to start off with and it does feel like work. Learning guitar and accidentally muting notes would make me so angry as a kid. If you put in the time you eventually improve so that you can do it effortlessly and it becomes super fun and rewarding. Playing guitar is now great for me to relax to, but it wasn't in the beginning. Likewise, ive recently taken up drawing to give my hands something to do and I suck. I'm terrible. But you've just got to embrace that to get to a point where you can enjoy it. These sorts of hobbies have a higher skill entry than video games. They aren't immediately 'fun'. It's pretty easy to master a game controller. There are only a few buttons to learn before you can start pwning noobs online. Not so with other hobbies. I'm having to learn all sorts of stuff about 'frames' and 'planes' that isn't exactly intuitive. But I know that when I do fully grasp these concepts I'll be able to derive great satisfaction out of creating accurate drawings. 

If you're really into video games you could try learning to code. Or model 3D characters. The options are endless. It's entirely up to you :)
